title: Niacinamide vs Hyaluronic Acid: Differences and How to Use Both
ex: Hyaluronic acid hydrates; niacinamide balances oil and supports the barrier. See which suits your skin type and how to layer them in Indian weather.
rt: Niacinamide vs Hyaluronic Acid: Which First? | Mirc Glow
rd: Niacinamide vs hyaluronic acid: what each one does, which suits oily, dry or sensitive skin, how to layer them, and tips for humid weather and AC rooms.
quick: Hyaluronic acid is a hydrator that holds water in the skin so it looks plumper. Niacinamide (vitamin B3) helps balance oil, helps pores look smaller and supports the barrier. They do not conflict: apply the thinner product first, then moisturiser at night or sunscreen in the morning.
facts: Hyaluronic acid is a humectant that draws and holds water.
Niacinamide is often used at around 2–5% in creams.
The two can be layered or used in one product.
Mirc Glow Glass Glow Cream contains both niacinamide and hyaluronic acid.
